blocks.text:
After breakfast, drive about three and a half hours to the Angra dos Reis area, then take a boat to Ilha Grande. Check in at your hotel on arrival and take some time to rest.

Most of the island is protected. There are no cars, so you travel between bays on foot or by boat. Ilha Grande was once home to a penal colony and a maximum-security prison, which closed in the 1990s. Today, life centres on the waterfront, with small pousadas, wooden jetties, fishing boats, restaurants and bars.

Local restaurants serve moqueca, a thick fish stew with coconut milk, lime and coriander. Beaches alternate with forest, granite slopes and clear bays where sea turtles and tropical fish can be seen.

blocks.text:
After breakfast, take a boat along the island's coast to beaches and small bays that are easiest to reach from the water. Between stops, you'll pass green islets and thickly forested slopes, with the water changing from deep blue to clear green.

At the stops, you can snorkel or relax on the sand. Dolphins, sea turtles and large tropical fish are found in the bay. After the busy days in Rio, the pace changes here. There are few roads and little city bustle, with the ocean, forest and boats moored at the jetties all around.
